classification.method: fixed host: every load is a new process (cold); no restore exists; warm = the same process's later requests

conclusion: FIXED HOST, NOT LAMBDA. 0xd40 local-file: load 7.934 -> 2.279 s (-5.649, 5/5 rounds, p1 spread 0.056); memfd -5.666 s. Warm, first inference, 4,096-token forward and peak RSS no change. Answers bit-identical to P1 (50/50 requests, 10/10 forwards). x86_64: KleidiAI cannot be compiled, the change is not in the binary path; every metric no change, answers identical to x86 P1. Dormant (patched libs, switch unset): load +0.058 s against p1's 0.056 s range, answers identical: a 0.7% residue at the edge of the spread, recorded, not a regression of the default. Verdict: general default, with threads = the engine's thread count (the shipped switch value 6 matched THREADS=6 here).

conditions.note: FIXED HOST, NOT LAMBDA LATENCY. One fresh container per load; arms interleaved by cyclic rotation of one round's order; comparisons pair rounds (arm minus p1 in the same round).

cost.note: fixed host already provisioned; no AWS calls

functions.note: memory_mb is P1's Lambda setting, kept for the schema; the container has no memory limit (cgroup memory.max as recorded per load)

hypothesis: Six-thread KleidiAI load-time repack (GGML_KLEIDIAI_REPACK_THREADS=6) removes the serial repack cost off Lambda too, with no warm/forward/memory or answer change, and is inert where KleidiAI is absent (x86_64).
